_note: Analyst-perspective quality rubric, adapted from O*NET task-statement review criteria. STARTING POINT — refine the criteria/wording with Phil. Binary per criterion; the judge returns pass/fail + a short reason for each. Pass rates get Wilson CIs.

criteria.label: Face validity
criteria.question: Does the statement describe genuine, relevant work that someone in this occupation actually performs (not idiosyncratic, outdated, or out-of-scope)?

criteria.label: Single coherent activity
criteria.question: Does it describe a single COHERENT work activity? IMPORTANT: enumerated examples or facets of one activity PASS (e.g. 'debug and fix issues such as code errors, database problems, and bugs' is one activity — debugging — with examples; 'review PRs and provide feedback' is one activity — reviewing). FAIL ONLY when genuinely DISTINCT activities are conjoined into one statement (e.g. 'develop or direct testing procedures, programming, or documentation' bundles testing + programming + documentation; 'modify software to correct errors, adapt to new hardware, or upgrade interfaces' bundles distinct tasks).

criteria.label: Appropriate generality
criteria.question: Is it written at an appropriate level of generality — neither a vague umbrella that covers many different activities, nor a trivial micro-step?

criteria.label: Clarity / self-contained
criteria.question: Is it clear, unambiguous, and understandable on its own without additional context or jargon?

criteria.label: Action-oriented
criteria.question: Does it begin with an action verb and describe an observable work activity (what the worker does)?
